replication.target_description: Same OSF project, author final accepted 2023 manuscript: preregistered decision-quality analysis, main effect of successful versus failed outcome in 2 outcome x 2 decision-maker between-participant ANOVA; 692 MTurk participants after exclusions.

n.sample_role: Participants in the post-exclusion 2x2 ANOVA of decision quality (344 success, 348 failure; residual df=688).
n.exclusions: 707 recruited; 2 incomplete surveys excluded, then 13 excluded under the other preregistered criteria: low English proficiency (<5/7), low seriousness (<4/5), or correctly guessing the hypothesis. All questions forced response; no missing data.

notes: Original title verified as Outcome Bias in Decision Evaluation; original PDF acquired from University of Florida faculty-hosted copy. Original cached OCR reads r(19) at the aggregate t statistic; the test is identified as paired t in the supplied author preregistration and the final replication manuscript discussion. Requested test-statistic metric retained for both sides; replication also prints Cohen’s f = .47, 90% CI [.40, .53], which is not substituted for F. Original aggregate covers seven matched case pairs; replication focuses on the heart-surgery scenario, with design changed from within to between participants. Supplied replication cache is a revised preregistration, not a results report; its planned N and calculated original-condition statistics were not used as replication results. Independently obtained final accepted manuscript from this same OSF project (https://osf.io/download/avzqw/), title and authors verified, DOI 10.5334/irsp.751. This version was accepted June 27, 2023; relevant result is on printed p.18 rather than supplied locator p.6. The locator is interpreted as the neutral description’s overall outcome contrast, not the decision-maker main effect, interaction or subgroup contrasts. target_match refers to this overall outcome-bias contrast and project identity; original and replication intentionally differ in experimental design and scenario coverage.
